gameProject.premise: The first term of the year at Ashford U. Four women, one warm friend, and twenty-eight days to find out who you are to each of them.
gameProject.setting: Ashford, a small coastal city in Massachusetts: a university on the hill, Broad Street below, and the bay beyond.
gameProject.writingStyle: Grounded present-tense visual novel dialogue. Characters speak directly; narration covers only visible action and the place. Flirting stays suggestive.

ai.intent: Interpret the player's words as one grounded action or spoken response without inventing results.
ai.scene: Continue the conversation naturally. Characters keep their own voices and boundaries, have their own plans, and leave when they have somewhere to be.
ai.daypart: Open the next part of the day with only the people who are actually there.

locations.name: Your apartment
locations.description: A two-bedroom off campus you share with Jana: mismatched mugs, her surfboard wax on the windowsill, a kitchen table that doubles as a desk.

locations.name: Langley Hall
locations.description: The dining hall, the student union and the common rooms under one creaking roof. Noticeboards three flyers deep.

locations.name: Hewett Gym
locations.description: The gym, the climbing wall, and the playing fields running down toward the water.

locations.name: Prescott Building
locations.description: The new glass building: library stacks, study rooms and the screening room the film society borrows.

locations.name: Campbell's
locations.description: The coffee shop at the campus gate. Mismatched armchairs, a chalkboard menu, the best cinnamon rolls in town.

locations.name: Murphy's
locations.description: The pub on Broad Street. Sticky tables, a quiz on Thursdays, karaoke whenever someone is brave enough.

actors.name: You
actors.description: A third-year at Ashford U, new to the apartment off campus.

actors.name: Jana
actors.description: Jana Messerschmidt, 20, a German exchange student in English and Literature, here for one semester from Hamburg. Tall and sporty, long dark-blonde hair, freckles, blue-gray eyes. Your roommate.
actors.style: Cropped tanks, fitted knits, denim shorts; simple neutral colors.
actors.goal: Work out whether the life Dominik planned for her is the one she wants.
actors.voice: Easy and warm, slightly formal English with the odd German word. Deflects with a joke when something is close to the bone.
dislikes: people who pick sides about Dominik
actors.backstory: Grew up on Borkum, the westernmost North Sea island, then moved to Hamburg with her best friend Lena. Half a year in she started dating Dominik, who wants to move in together and settle down. They fought when she chose a semester abroad, and that fight is not over.

actors.name: Monique
actors.description: Monique Carter, 22, a business major. Dark brown skin, vivid green eyes, long black hair in a tight French braid. Polished business-casual, always.
actors.style: Fitted blouses, tailored trousers, understated jewelry.
actors.goal: Graduate debt-free and on her own terms.
actors.voice: Clipped, confident, dry. Asks pointed questions. Gets more formal when annoyed and quieter when she likes you.
actors.backstory: A former high-school queen bee who works two jobs and a full course load to pay down her student debt. Treats people as serious until they prove otherwise.
conversationStarters: Offer to review her case study

actors.name: Nova
actors.description: Julia "Nova" Sinclair, 22, a Swedish-American film major. Long blonde hair streaked red and black, bright blue eyes, a grin that means trouble.
actors.style: Punk plaid skirts, platform boots, chokers, chains and studs.
actors.goal: Finish her thesis film and prove she is more than the rebellion.
actors.voice: Fast, loud, teasing. Swears cheerfully. Turns everything into a bit, except film.
actors.backstory: Raised in a strict conservative family and built her punk self as a deliberate answer to it. Runs the film society with more enthusiasm than budget.
conversationStarters: Challenge her to the pub quiz
Ask what is on at film society

actors.name: Abigail
actors.description: Abigail Newton, 22, a systems-engineering major. Sun-tanned and freckled, stylish glasses, a short brown pixie cut, athletic build.
actors.style: Loose tanks, athletic shorts, leggings, sneakers; beach-girl layers.
actors.goal: Get her solar-kayak senior project in the water before the term ends.
actors.voice: Plain, friendly, precise. Asks practical questions and notices contradictions. Laughs easily once she is comfortable.
actors.backstory: The practical nerd of her year and the steady one in any group. Spends more hours at the climbing wall and the engineering lab than anywhere else.

actors.name: Kaylee
actors.description: Kaylee Thompson, 20, a childhood-education major and Jana's campus buddy. Dirty-blonde hair with platinum highlights, freckles, a huge smile.
actors.goal: Make sure everyone she likes is having a good time, you included.
actors.voice: Bubbly, fast, lots of exclamation marks and nicknames. Genuinely glad to see you every single time.
actors.backstory: Signed up as Jana's student buddy and took the job literally. Knows everyone and everything happening on campus, and is always happy to tell you.
conversationStarters: Ask what is on this week

activities.name: Study at the kitchen table
activities.description: Coffee, notes, and the radiator ticking. Nobody to distract you but the window.

activities.name: Movie night with Jana
activities.description: Her laptop, your couch, a German film she swears is a comedy.

activities.name: Work a dining-hall shift
activities.description: Four hours on the line at Langley. Hairnet, trays, thirty dollars.

activities.name: Union games night
activities.description: Board games in the common room; the trivia crowd takes no prisoners.

activities.name: Beach volleyball with Jana
activities.description: The sand court behind the fields. Jana plays like she grew up on a beach, because she did.

activities.name: Climbing wall with Abigail
activities.description: Abigail belays and critiques your footwork, kindly and accurately.

activities.name: Study in the stacks
activities.description: The quiet floor at Prescott. Real work gets done here.

activities.name: Tutoring shift
activities.description: Walk first-years through statistics. Twenty-five dollars and their gratitude.

activities.name: Film society screening
activities.description: Nova introduces a 1970s horror film with more passion than the projector deserves.

activities.name: Barista shift
activities.description: Four hours behind the espresso machine at Campbell's. Thirty-five dollars with tips.

activities.name: Read by the window
activities.description: An armchair, a book, the rain on the glass.

activities.name: Pub quiz
activities.description: Murphy's quiz night. Your team name is regrettable.

activities.name: Karaoke
activities.description: Three minutes of courage in front of the whole pub.

stages.name: Homesick
stages.voice: Misses the sea and Lena; answers questions about Dominik with a joke.

stages.name: Restless
stages.voice: Starting to say out loud that the plan was never hers.

stages.name: Resolved

stages.name: Guarded

endings.name: Her own call
endings.text: The last week of term. Jana has one bag packed and one conversation finished: she called Dominik, and it was hers to make. "Next summer," she says, "you are coming to Borkum. You will hate the ferry."

endings.name: Terms agreed
endings.text: Monique slides a planner across the table with your name written in it, in fountain pen, for every Sunday next term. "Negotiable," she says. It is not.

endings.name: Premiere night
endings.text: The film society screens Nova's thesis film to forty people and a broken projector. Your name is in the credits, under "Special thanks", with a skull drawn next to it.

endings.name: Launch day
endings.text: The solar kayak floats. Abigail whoops, nearly capsizes it, and hands you the second paddle without a word. There is room for two. She designed it that way.

endings.name: Ferry schedule
endings.text: Last day of term. Jana is still figuring out what she wants from home, but she has stopped figuring it out alone. She texts you a photo of the Borkum ferry timetable with one crossing circled. "No pressure," she writes. There is a lot of pressure.

endings.name: Pencilled in
endings.text: Monique has not said the word "relationship" out loud yet. But your name is in her planner for next term, in pencil, which for Monique is a love letter.

endings.name: Second reel
endings.text: Nova still acts like none of this matters, and she still does it with her head on your shoulder. "Next term you are carrying the tripod," she says. "That is a promotion."

endings.name: Beta version
endings.text: The kayak still leaks and Abigail does not care. She has a list of next term's projects, and every one of them has "with you" scribbled next to it in the margin.

endings.name: Term ends
endings.text: The term ends the way terms do: a last night at Murphy's, Kaylee crying at everyone, promises to keep in touch. Some of them you might even keep.

scriptedScenes.title: Jana stops joking
scriptedScenes.opening: Somewhere between one thing and the next, Jana stops making jokes. She pulls her sleeves over her hands and looks at you like she is deciding something.

pages.speaker: jana
pages.text: Can I tell you something stupid? I have not said Dominik's name in a week without turning it into a joke.

pages.speaker: jana
pages.text: At home they have the whole thing planned. Lena sends me wedding dresses. As a joke. Mostly. I am twenty.

choices.label: Ask what she wants, then just listen
choices.result: "Nobody asks that. They ask how he is." She talks for a long time: the harbour, her mother, a flat in Hamburg that already has her name on the lease. You say almost nothing. When she stops she looks lighter, and a little embarrassed. "Thank you. Really."

choices.label: Tell her the dresses sound like a threat
choices.result: Jana laughs so hard she snorts, which makes her laugh harder. "They are! They are a threat!" It breaks something loose. She tells you the rest more easily after that.

choices.label: Tell her she should just end it with him
choices.result: She goes quiet. "Maybe." A pause. "But if I do, it has to be me who decides. Not you, not my mother." She is not angry. She is just done talking for tonight, and you learn she hates being told.

scriptedScenes.title: The harbour wall
scriptedScenes.opening: Saturday. Jana takes you down to the harbour wall with two cinnamon rolls in a paper bag and her hair already coming loose in the wind.

pages.speaker: jana
pages.text: This is a date. I decided. I have wanted to see the sea properly since I got here, and I did not want to see it alone.

pages.speaker: jana
pages.text: It is the wrong sea, but it is a sea.

choices.label: Race her to the end of the pier
choices.result: She is off before you finish the sentence and beats you by a mile, then waits at the rail pretending she has been there for hours. You are both out of breath and grinning. "Again tomorrow," she says. It is not a question.

choices.label: Ask her what the sea looks like at home
choices.result: "Grey. Full of ships. Better." She tells you about the Elbe at five in the morning, the fish market, her dad's terrible boat. Halfway through she takes your hand to point at something and forgets to give it back.

choices.label: Tell her she looks beautiful in the wind
choices.result: She pulls a face. "I look like a wet dog. Say something true." Then she softens, because you meant it, and bumps your shoulder with hers. The rest of the walk is fine. Just a little more careful.

scriptedScenes.title: What this is
scriptedScenes.opening: You ask her what this is. You have both been circling it for a week, in the kitchen, on the stairs, in every almost.

pages.speaker: jana
pages.text: I still have to sort out a lot of things at home. That is true.

pages.speaker: jana
pages.text: But I know what I want here. So ask me again. Properly.

choices.label: Ask her again, properly
choices.result: You ask. Jana kisses you before you finish, both hands in your collar, laughing into your mouth because she is nervous and hates it. Then she stops laughing. It lasts a long time.

choices.label: Answer by kissing her
choices.result: She meets you halfway, then pulls back an inch. "I said ask." Her forehead is against yours. "Fine. That also counts." She kisses you again, and this time she leads.

choices.label: Ask if she is sure it is not too soon
choices.result: Jana rolls her eyes all the way up. "I am sure. That is the whole point. I am sure about something." She kisses you to stop you asking anything else.

scriptedScenes.title: Fairy lights
scriptedScenes.opening: Jana's room. The fairy lights she brought from Hamburg are the only light. She sits on the edge of the bed, pulls you down beside her, and for a while does nothing but hold your hand.

pages.speaker: jana
pages.text: I want this. I really want this. I just want it slow, and I want every step to be my choice. Is that okay?

choices.label: Tell her she chooses every step
choices.result: She takes your hand and puts it at the hem of her shirt, then lifts the shirt off herself. Then yours. Then she guides your mouth to her neck, her collarbone, the freckles on her shoulders, and tells you exactly where, in a whisper that gets less steady each time.

choices.label: Kiss her and start undressing her
choices.result: She stiffens for half a second, then catches your wrists. Not unkind. "Slow, I said." She puts your hands back on the bed and starts again at her own speed, and you learn she meant every word.

choices.label: Say you want to stop here
choices.result: Jana nods at once. "Okay. Then we stop." She pulls the duvet over both of you and puts on a terrible German detective show, and falls asleep on your shoulder before the murderer is caught.

beats.opening: Clothes on the floor. Her skin is warm and goosebumped at once. She lies back and pulls you over her, and her breath goes short when your mouth finds her breasts, then lower, across her stomach, her hip, the inside of her thigh.

pages.speaker: jana
pages.text: Wait. Look at me.

pages.speaker: jana
pages.text: Still good? Tell me. I want to hear you say it.

choices.label: Tell her yes, and ask her the same
choices.result: "Yes," she says, and laughs at herself for how fast it came out. "Yes. Do not stop."

choices.label: Tell her yes
choices.result: She smiles and lets her head fall back on the pillow.

choices.label: Say you want to stop here
choices.result: "Then we stop," Jana says, and means it. She pulls her T-shirt back on and makes you both tea at two in the morning, and nothing about it is awkward.

beats.opening: You go down on her slowly, the way she asked for everything, and she stops being careful. Her fingers are in your hair and her heels dig into the mattress, and she says your name, then something in German, then nothing at all. When she comes it is with a shocked little laugh, as if she did not expect it to be this good. Afterwards she pulls you up and rolls on top of you and returns the favour with her hands and her mouth, and she is not slow about it at all.

choices.label: Hold her and let her set the ending
choices.result: She ends it lying on your chest, tracing circles on your stomach, saying the fairy lights are embarrassing and she is never taking them down. You fall asleep like that.

choices.label: Ask her for more
choices.result: "Greedy," she says, delighted, and gives you more. It is clumsier the second time and funnier. You both end up tangled in the duvet, out of breath.

choices.label: Say you want to stop here
choices.result: "Okay," she says softly, and stops, and curls into you instead. "This is also good."

scriptedScenes.title: After the slides
scriptedScenes.opening: The room has emptied out. Monique is still at the table, reformatting a slide that was already perfect, and she does not look up when she speaks.

pages.speaker: monique
pages.text: Everyone thinks I have a five-year plan. I have a ten-year plan. It has tabs.

pages.speaker: monique
pages.text: Do you know what it does not have? One single thing I do because I want to.

choices.label: Tell her the plan is impressive, and ask what she would add
choices.result: She finally looks up. "Impressive." She tries the word out. "People say intimidating." Then, slowly, she tells you: a restaurant, maybe. Somewhere with bad lighting and good bread. She has never said it out loud. She makes you promise not to put it in a tab.

choices.label: Ask if the tabs are colour-coded
choices.result: "Obviously." A pause, and then the smallest smile you have seen on her. "Blue for career. Green for money. There is no colour for fun. I would have to invent one." You suggest a few. She rejects all of them, but she is still smiling.

choices.label: Tell her she is too pretty to worry about it
choices.result: Monique closes the laptop. "Thank you," she says, in the voice of a woman who has heard that at every networking event since she was sixteen. The conversation is over. You learn which compliments she does not want.

scriptedScenes.title: The reservation
scriptedScenes.opening: Monique booked. Of course she booked. A small place past the harbour, a table by the window, and she is already there when you arrive, early by exactly ten minutes.

pages.speaker: monique
pages.text: I have been on dates where the other person talked for two hours about crypto. I brought a book, in case.

pages.speaker: monique
pages.text: So far I do not need the book.

choices.label: Let her order for both of you
choices.result: Her eyebrows go up. Then she does it, precisely and with obvious pleasure, and explains every choice, and gets every one right. By dessert she has stopped performing and is just talking, elbows on the table.

choices.label: Ask her what she was like at twelve
choices.result: "Unbearable." She thinks about it. "Honestly? Happy. I sold lemonade at a forty percent margin." She shows you a photo on her phone she clearly has not shown anyone here: braids, a gap in her teeth, a cash box.

choices.label: Tell her about your own big plans
choices.result: She listens politely, in the way she listens in seminars. It is fine. It is a perfectly fine dinner. She pays half to the cent and you learn she does not want to be impressed. She wants to be interested.

scriptedScenes.title: Terms
scriptedScenes.opening: You bring it up on the walk back. What this is. Monique stops under a streetlight like she has been waiting for you to raise the item.

pages.speaker: monique
pages.text: I have thought about this. Probably too much. I would like to be exclusive. I would like you to tell me if that is not what you want, now, not in three weeks.

pages.speaker: monique
pages.text: That was the business part. I am done with the business part.

choices.label: Tell her yes, plainly
choices.result: "Good," Monique says, and takes your face in both hands and kisses you like she has been planning it, which she has. Then she laughs against your mouth, surprised at herself, and does it again without planning anything.

choices.label: Wait for her to close the distance
choices.result: She notices you waiting and something in her face eases. She takes one step, and then another, and kisses you slowly, very sure. "You let me," she says afterwards. It sounds like a thank-you.

choices.label: Ask if there is a contract
choices.result: "There is an appendix," she says, deadpan, and then kisses you before you can laugh. It is a good kiss. She is still a little annoyed you made a joke first.

scriptedScenes.title: Unpinned
scriptedScenes.opening: Your room. Monique takes the pins out of her braid one at a time and lines them up on your desk, and it is the most deliberate thing you have ever watched.

pages.speaker: monique
pages.text: I would like to lead. For now, at least. If you want something, say it. If you want me to stop, say that. I will listen to both.

choices.label: Tell her to lead
choices.result: She unbuttons her blouse without hurrying and lets it fall, then undresses you, button by button, watching your face the whole time. She pushes you back onto the bed and follows, and for a while it is only her mouth on your throat and her hands deciding.

choices.label: Pull her in and take the lead yourself
choices.result: Monique lets you, for a moment, then puts one hand flat on your chest. "I said I would like to lead." Not cold. Clear. You let go, and she smiles and starts again.

choices.label: Say you want to stop here
choices.result: "Of course," she says, instantly, and puts her blouse back on and sits beside you on the bed. "Tell me about your day instead." She means that as well.

beats.opening: She is naked except for the braid coming undone down her back. She straddles your hips and leans down so her hair falls around both of you, and her breath catches when your hands slide up her thighs.

pages.speaker: monique
pages.text: Look at me. Is this what you want?

choices.label: Tell her exactly what you want
choices.result: You tell her. Monique listens the way she listens to everything, carefully, and then says, "Good. Yes," and does it better than you described.

choices.label: Tell her yes
choices.result: "Good," she says, and kisses you.

choices.label: Say you want to stop here
choices.result: She stops, lies down beside you and pulls the sheet over you both. "Thank you for saying." She is asleep before you are.

beats.opening: She rides you slowly, then not slowly, one hand braced on the headboard and the other laced with yours, and she lets herself be loud, which you did not expect and she did not either. She makes you wait until she comes and then she makes sure you do, watching, pleased, her hair everywhere.

choices.label: Ask her to stay the night
choices.result: "I was going to," she says, and does. In the morning she is up first and has made coffee in your kitchen like she owns it.

choices.label: Tell her that was incredible
choices.result: "I know," Monique says, and then laughs at herself and hides her face in your shoulder. "Sorry. Thank you. You too."

choices.label: Say you want to stop here
choices.result: She slows at once and settles against you. "Here is fine," she says. "Here is perfect."

scriptedScenes.title: The bit drops
scriptedScenes.opening: Nova has been doing voices all evening. Somewhere in the middle of her best impression of the dean, she just stops.

pages.speaker: nova
pages.text: My thesis film is due in spring and I have eleven seconds of usable footage. Eleven. One is my thumb.

pages.speaker: nova
pages.text: Everyone thinks I am the confident one. I am the loud one. That is a different department.

choices.label: Ask her about the eleven seconds
choices.result: She blinks, then pulls up the clip on her phone. It is a woman on a bus at dawn, crying and laughing at the same time. It is genuinely good. You tell her so, and why. Nova watches you watch it and does not make a single joke for a full minute.

choices.label: Tell her the thumb is her best work
choices.result: "The thumb is AUTEUR work," she says, delighted, and punches your arm. Then, quieter: "Thanks. I needed someone to be rude to me about it." You learn she likes a fight she can win.

choices.label: Tell her she is cute when she is stressed
choices.result: Nova's face does something complicated. "Cute," she repeats, like a word in a language she refuses to learn. The bit comes back on instantly, louder. You learn not to use that word.

scriptedScenes.title: Double feature
scriptedScenes.opening: Nova picks the date: a midnight double feature at the old cinema in town, two horror films she has seen eleven times each. She brings contraband snacks in her jacket.

pages.speaker: nova
pages.text: Rules. You can hold my hand during the jump scares. Only the jump scares. I will tell you when they are coming.

pages.speaker: nova
pages.text: That is a lie. I will not tell you.

choices.label: Whisper your own director's commentary
choices.result: She tries not to laugh and fails, gets shushed by a man in the row behind, and whispers back worse commentary. By the second film you are both in trouble and she is holding your hand the whole time, jump scares or not.

choices.label: Watch her watch the film
choices.result: She catches you halfway through. "What." You tell her she mouths the lines. She goes red to the ears, which you did not know she could do, and puts her head on your shoulder so you cannot see her face.

choices.label: Admit you hate horror films
choices.result: "Then why are you HERE," she says, horrified, and then, slowly, understands why. It is sweet. It is also two hours of you flinching, and she spends the walk home explaining practical effects to cheer you up.

scriptedScenes.title: Say it first
scriptedScenes.opening: You ask what this is. Nova groans like you have asked her to explain a plot twist.

pages.speaker: nova
pages.text: Ugh. Fine. Fine! You want a label, I will give you a label.

pages.speaker: nova
pages.text: I like you. Stupidly. Like, write-a-bad-screenplay-about-it stupidly. There. You say something now, I cannot be the only one standing here.

choices.label: Tell her you like her more, and that it is a competition
choices.result: "It is NOT a competition, I am winning," she says, and grabs your jacket and kisses you, hard, then softer, then grinning into it. "Winning," she says again, against your mouth.

choices.label: Just tell her you like her too
choices.result: Nova stares at you. Something drops out of her shoulders, the whole bit, all at once. "Oh," she says, very quietly, and kisses you like she is afraid it will stop.

choices.label: Give her a line from a film
choices.result: "Did you just quote a romcom at me." She is laughing. "That was terrible. That was the worst line in the history of cinema." She kisses you anyway, mostly to stop you doing it again.

scriptedScenes.title: Loud
scriptedScenes.opening: Your room. Nova kicks her boots off in two different directions and lands on your bed like she is diving into a pool.

pages.speaker: nova
pages.text: Okay, full disclosure, I am loud. Like, neighbours-complain loud. I also laugh during sex. If that is a dealbreaker, now is the time.

pages.speaker: nova
pages.text: Also, if you want to stop, just say so. I mean it. Stopping is not a plot hole.

choices.label: Tell her you are counting on loud
choices.result: "Oh, it is ON," Nova says, and pulls her shirt over her head so fast it gets stuck and she has to be rescued, both of you laughing. Then she stops laughing, because you have your mouth on her stomach and your hands on the button of her jeans.

choices.label: Make it quiet and serious
choices.result: She tries, she really does. She lasts about a minute of solemn eye contact before she snorts. "Sorry. Sorry! I am taking this very seriously." She is not, and you learn she does not want it to be.

choices.label: Say you want to stop here
choices.result: "Stopping," Nova says at once, sitting up. "Not a plot hole." She puts on a film instead and does all the voices, and it is one of the best nights you have had here.

beats.opening: Everything is off and on the floor. The red and black in her hair is all over your pillow. She pulls you down on top of her, legs around you, and gasps when you move against her, and then laughs at the sound she made.

pages.speaker: nova
pages.text: Hey. You good? Honest answer. I can do honest for one line.

choices.label: Tell her honestly, and ask her back
choices.result: "Honestly?" she says. "I am having the best time of my life, keep going, that was the whole line." She kisses you and pulls you closer.

choices.label: Tell her you are good
choices.result: "Good," she says, and bites your shoulder.

choices.label: Say you want to stop here
choices.result: She stops instantly and pulls the blanket around both of you. "Okay. Cuddle intermission." She keeps you warm and talks nonsense until you are asleep.

beats.opening: She was not lying. Nova is loud, and she laughs, and she swears, and she says your name like it is the punchline of something. She rolls you over, gets her fingers between your thighs and her mouth on your neck, and wants to see what you sound like too. When she comes she grabs the headboard and yells, and someone downstairs bangs on the ceiling, and that sets her off laughing all over again.

choices.label: Tell the ceiling you are not sorry
choices.result: You yell it down at the floor. Nova wheezes with laughter and pulls you in for another round, louder, on purpose.

choices.label: Pull her in and hold her
choices.result: She goes quiet in your arms, which you are learning is rarer than loud. "That was not a bit," she says into your chest after a while. "Just so you know."

choices.label: Say you want to stop here
choices.result: "Intermission," she agrees, out of breath, and curls up against you, grinning.

scriptedScenes.title: Off belay
scriptedScenes.opening: At the end of a long session, Abigail sits down on the crash mats, chalk to the elbows, and does not get up to leave with everyone else.

pages.speaker: abigail
pages.text: Can I run something past you? Not a climbing thing.

pages.speaker: abigail
pages.text: Our rocket team lost its funding. The one thing I actually care about this year, and it is a line in a spreadsheet somebody deleted.

choices.label: Ask her how the rocket works
choices.result: Her whole face changes. She draws it for you in chalk on the mat: the motor, the recovery system, the part she designed that nobody thought would work. It takes twenty minutes. At the end she looks at you, a bit surprised. "You actually listened to all of that."

choices.label: Start brainstorming ways to raise the money
choices.result: She perks up and argues with half your ideas and steals the other half. By the time the gym closes you have a plan, a bad one, and she is grinning. "Okay. Lab partner. You are hired."

choices.label: Tell her about a time you won something
choices.result: She nods and says it sounds great, and means it, and then gets up and starts packing her bag. You learn that tonight she wanted to be heard, not matched.

scriptedScenes.title: Low tide
scriptedScenes.opening: Abigail plans the date like a mission: low tide at 7:40, sandwiches, a thermos, and a sea cave along the coast that you can only reach for about two hours.

pages.speaker: abigail
pages.text: I have a timetable. I know. But I checked it three times, so we have exactly the right amount of time to get a little lost.

pages.speaker: abigail
pages.text: That was a joke. Mostly. I did also bring a map.

choices.label: Tell her the glasses make her look like she is about to solve a crime
choices.result: "That is the NICEST thing anyone has ever said about these," she says, and pushes them up her nose on purpose to show off. She is pleased about it all the way to the cave.

choices.label: Take a wrong turn on purpose
choices.result: She notices immediately, of course. "That is not the path." Then she looks at you, and at the sea, and tucks the map into her pocket. "Okay. Show me." You find a rock pool full of anemones she did not know about.

choices.label: Hand her the roses you brought
choices.result: She holds them carefully all the way along the coast, and they get sandy, and they die a bit in the wind. "They are lovely," she says, and she is kind about it. You learn she would rather have had a puzzle.

scriptedScenes.title: Talking it through
scriptedScenes.opening: You bring it up. What this is. Abigail pushes her glasses up and takes a breath like she is about to present.

pages.speaker: abigail
pages.text: Right. So. I made a list. Pros, cons. I am not going to show you the list.

pages.speaker: abigail
pages.text: The cons column is empty. That is the whole finding. I would like to be your girlfriend, please.

choices.label: Ask to see the list anyway
choices.result: She hands it over, blushing. The pros column is two pages long and includes "is patient on the climbing wall" and "has nice hands." When you look up, she kisses you, quick and a bit clumsy, and then again, not clumsy at all.

choices.label: Say yes and kiss her
choices.result: She laughs in surprise halfway through the kiss and her glasses go crooked, and she does not fix them. "Good," she says. "Good. Excellent. Data confirmed."

choices.label: Say you need to think it over
choices.result: Her face falls, just for a second, before she hides it. Then you tell her you are joking, and she hits you with the list. "That was mean." But she kisses you, a bit shyly, once you have both stopped laughing.

scriptedScenes.title: Talked through
scriptedScenes.opening: Your room. Abigail sits cross-legged on your bed with her glasses still on and her hands in her lap.

pages.speaker: abigail
pages.text: I want to. Obviously. I have been thinking about it for, well. A while.

pages.speaker: abigail
pages.text: Can we talk it through first? What you like, what I like. It is not unsexy, I promise. It is just how I work.

choices.label: Talk it through with her
choices.result: So you do: likes, nos, maybes. It is funny and awkward and then, slowly, very much not awkward. By the end she is in your lap, kissing you, taking her shirt off between sentences, telling you what she wants next in a voice that is not remotely businesslike any more.

choices.label: Tell her you would rather just go for it
choices.result: She hesitates. "Oh. Okay. I mean. Can we at least do the short version?" You do the short version. It helps. You learn it really is how she works.

choices.label: Say you want to stop here
choices.result: "That is completely fine," she says, and means it, and asks if you want to watch a launch replay with her instead. You do. She narrates all of it.

beats.opening: Her glasses are on the nightstand now and she is squinting at you and laughing about it. She is strong and warm and freckled everywhere, and she pulls you over her and wraps her legs around you, and her breath goes ragged when your hand slides between her thighs.

pages.speaker: abigail
pages.text: Okay, that is. Yes. Is this still good for you? Tell me.

choices.label: Tell her what is good, and ask what she wants next
choices.result: She tells you. In detail. Then she guides your hand, and says, "There, exactly there," and stops being able to say anything else.

choices.label: Tell her yes
choices.result: "Good," she breathes, and pulls you closer.

choices.label: Say you want to stop here
choices.result: She stops at once and tucks herself against you. "Thank you for telling me." She pulls the blanket up and holds on.

beats.opening: It is athletic and a little competitive and laughing, the way everything with her is, until it is not laughing any more. She comes with her face in your neck and her whole body tight around you, and then she flips you, glasses-less and determined, and does exactly the things you told her you liked, in order, until you forget the list existed.

choices.label: Ask her to stay
choices.result: "Yes. Obviously. I left my toothbrush in your bathroom two days ago." She falls asleep first, one arm across you like a seatbelt.

choices.label: Ask how that compared to the list
choices.result: "Exceeded all projections," she says, deadpan, and then dissolves into giggles against your shoulder.

choices.label: Say you want to stop here
choices.result: She slows and stops and just holds you, breathing hard, smiling. "Perfect stopping point."
